claim: Claim A — the system compares different foundation-model readings of the same (M_ctx, Y_ctx) context; the four analytic properties (closed-form predictive variance, information gain, sequential update, Eckart-Young sensitivity) are not generic across them, and track M–Y-alignment retention together with c-recoverability.

columns.alignment_retained: 1 − cosine similarity under per-scenario y-shuffle (higher = uses M-Y joint assignment more)
columns.c_recoverability_in_linear / c_recoverab: joint R² of a linear c-probe (4 Wilson directions) fitted on training-scenario representations
columns.effective_rank: singular values above 1% of max, from repr_analysis diagnostics

ordering: rows sorted descending by alignment_retained; None last
global_caveats: fixed-ψ alignment and c-recoverability are computed fresh by this script (the model has no trainable parameters, so this is closed-form evaluation, not training)

scaled-JEPA alignment / c-recoverability / effective rank are from JEPA_summary_s in repr_analysis (same transformer architecture as the 186k/10k headline E_scale_all_jepa_tx_big but trained on 2k/6k); the 186k/10k held-out R² and parameter count are from output_jepa_scaling
constraint-violating regressor has architecturally undefined alignment and c-recoverability (it consumes c on the forward pass and has no Y_ctx slot); these cells are N/A by design

closed_form_predictive_variance.reason: ridge solve A = Ψᵀ Ψ + α I gives leverage(q) = ψ(q)ᵀ A⁻¹ ψ(q); predictive variance is σ_y² (1 + leverage)

closed_form_information_gain.reason: EPIG closed form follows from leverage via the matrix determinant lemma (paper Eq. 7 / INV-3 ΔH_D)

closed_form_sequential_update.reason: Sherman-Morrison rank-one update A_new⁻¹ = A⁻¹ − (A⁻¹ψ ψᵀ A⁻¹)/(1+lev) (paper Eq. 8)

eckart_young_sensitivity.reason: Eckart-Young bounds the sensitivity of A⁻¹ via its condition number; drift detector uses κ(A) directly
